issue_context.title: BUG: `df.to_excel` fails for `"border-style: hair"` with `xlsxwriter`
issue_context.body:
### Pandas version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the main branch of pandas.


### Reproducible Example

```python
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1]})
styler = df.style.applymap(lambda x: "border-style: hair; border-color: black")

styler.to_excel(r"test_border.xlsx", engine="xlsxwriter")
```


### Issue Description

The `CSSToExcelConverter._border_style` function does not return any value (i.e., None) when the style string is not recognized. However, "hair" should be a recognized style string in xlsxwriter, corresponding to [border index "7"](https://xlsxwriter.readthedocs.io/format.html#set_border). This leads to a crash in `xlsxwriter`. Moreover, there is no path to actually return the "hair" style for any engine.

### Expected Behavior

Use of `border-style: hair` will export a spreadsheet with the correct formatting.

comments: Thanks for the report @tehunter! Your versions indicate 1.5.0rc; do you know if this bug exists in previous versions?

I know that previous versions also had an inability to use the "hair" style. I'm unsure at the moment if it led to the same error. I think it probably gave the same error identified [here](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/42276#issuecomment-1007686150) and in #45312. 

In addition to adding support for the "hair" style, I think we probably need to have a "soft fail" for unrecognized/unimplemented border combinations. I'll work on adding both in a PR.

> However, "hair" should be a recognized style string in xlsxwriter, corresponding to [border index "1"](https://xlsxwriter.readthedocs.io/format.html#set_border)

Why not index 7? Does weight 0 mean that there is no visible border for index 7?
Yes, thanks for confirming. I misread the table; "hair" corresponds to index 7.

review_comments: Hmm why did this become case insensitive now? I though before it should have been explicit  (which was better IMO)?

[`CSSResolver.parse`](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blame/main/pandas/io/formats/css.py#L404) applies a lower-case conversion to all CSS properties and values. There's a TODO note from 6 years ago to not lowercase case-sensitive portions, but it looks like that still hasn't been implemented.

So if I do `styler.applymap(lambda x: "border-style: dashDotDot")`, the CSS parser converts that to a `("border-style", "dashdotdot")` tuple, and then the Excel formatter has to convert that back to `"dashDotDot"` so the engine code can set the border correctly

Given that CSS is case-insensitive already, I don't think the HTML-based formatters need to do case-lowering since the browser will interpret "solid" and "SOLID" the same, for example. I think that means we could move case translation out of the general CSS classes and into the Excel formatters where we can more easily control for case-sensitive values.
Wouldn't it be better to raise so the user can specify a supported style?

I believe the current code tends to prefer issuing `CSSWarning` instead of raising, such as in `CSSToExcelConverter.color_to_excel`.

From personal experience, it can be frustrating if the export code fails after doing expensive loading/manipulations to get to my final DataFrame, and then having to fix the error and repeat all over again. My thought is to export the file anyways and let the user decide if they want to rerun/reexport, or just clean up the formatting manually in Excel.
